messages:
sam (eng-sre): noticing sustained 2.4k rps to /v1/embeddings starting ~10:03 UTC, originating from ~12 IPs in a couple /24s. spike correlated with high 429s for customers. creating incident.

lina (sec): thanks — can you paste the top IPs and ASNs? also flag if tokens look scraped vs just brute force.

sam (eng-sre): top IPs 203.0.113.45, 203.0.113.67, 198.51.100.12. ASN 64500 and 64501. user-agent looks like "curl/7.86" and requests include long prompt param pattern repeated. not seeing valid auth failures — using valid API keys at high qps.

mike (oncall): applied temporary edge rate-limit (100 rps per key, 50 rps per ip) and turned on request-header challenge (x-edge-challenge). rolling WAF rule to block known probe pattern.

deploy-bot: WAF rule waf-811-deploy started in region us-west-1.

edge-bot: rate limit policy applied to route "/v1/embeddings" — global qps cap 2500, per-customer burst 300.

lina (sec): if they're using valid keys it looks like token scraping/abuse. we need KMS audit logs to see which service account performed those key minting/rotations. kate, are KMS audit logs on?

kate (platform): KMS admin logging is on for prod. I can pull logs — give me timeframe. note: rotating customer-managed keys will affect any Dedicated/private customers using that KMS.

sam (eng-sre): timeframe 10:00-10:10 UTC. also sending a snippet of request body pattern.

sam (eng-sre): ```
{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"[long repeated prompt pattern]","user":"unknown"}
```

lina (sec): thanks. I'll check vault/KMS activity and RBAC for any recently created service accounts or policy changes. if a compromised internal service account is leaking keys we should rotate and then update RBAC to lock down create/token permissions.

mike (oncall): applied WAF rule blocking request bodies matching "repeated prompt pattern" and blocked ASNs 64500-64501 at edge. seeing 75% drop in abusive RPS already.

elaine (cs): heads up — 3 enterprise customers reported increased 429s. drafting an incident-safe comms note. want to avoid saying keys compromised until we know.

lina (sec): agree. immediate action list: 1) confirm if abused keys belong to customers or internal service accounts 2) enable KMS key access audit filter for those keys 3) determine RBAC changes needed (deny key creation for non-admin SA) 4) rotate any compromised API keys and notify affected customers 5) run vuln triage on onboarding flow that mints keys.

kate (platform): running log query: gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyRingService.CreateCryptoKey\" AND timestamp>\"2026-03-12T10:00:00Z\"" --limit 50. returning results now.

kate (platform): result: one call from service-account:realtime-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 10:01 UTC, created a short-lived key.

lina (sec): mark that SA suspicious. who owns realtime-ingest?

sam (eng-sre): owned by eng-runtime team, used for telemetry ingestion. pinging runtime leads.

mike (oncall): runtime lead replied — they rotated telemetry keys yesterday per scheduled job. job config references an iam role that had broad key create perms.

lina (sec): root cause hypothesis: scheduled rotation job had overly broad RBAC, allowed key creation that was subsequently used by an internal service which leaked credentials to a third-party scraper. next steps: narrow RBAC, revoke the created key, rotate keys for impacted customers if theirs were used.

lina (sec): RBAC change proposal: remove roles/cloudkms.admin from non-admin SAs; add custom role cloudkms.keyAdmin-lite with only encrypt/decrypt/iam.get; restrict CreateCryptoKey to admin group. anyone object?

kate (platform): +1, will prepare minimal IAM delta and a rollback plan. toggling change via infra IaC (terraform) so we can roll back quickly.

mike (oncall): i've revoked the suspicious key id key-realtime-20260312 and blacklisted the API key used by the abusive requests at edge. monitoring for reuse.

deploy-bot: Edge blacklist applied for api-key id ak_live_0Xc... in region global.

lina (sec): please collect KMS audit export and S3 bucket of raw request logs for forensics. also capture a list of impacted customer API keys for comms.

sam (eng-sre): attaching small sample logs (sanitized) in thread.

sam (eng-sre): ```
10:04:02 INFO src=request_handler ip=203.0.113.45 api_key=ak_live_0Xc... model=text-embedding-3-small tokens=512 status=200
10:04:03 INFO src=request_handler ip=203.0.113.67 api_key=ak_live_0Xc... model=text-embedding-3-small tokens=512 status=200
```

elaine (cs): putting together outbound message: recommend customers rotate API keys if we confirm their key was used. draft: "we observed elevated usage patterns potentially indicating misuse; we have mitigations in place and recommend rotating keys as a precaution. more details to follow."

lina (sec): agree. don't call it a compromise yet. schedule postmortem: owner eng-runtime, invite eng-sre, platform, cs, legal. create JIRA INC-4521 for follow-ups (RBAC audit, KMS policy, key rotation playbook).

mike (oncall): monitoring trend — inbound RPS down to ~300 from abusive IPs, total 429s back to baseline. closing immediate mitigation in 1 hour unless we see resurgence.

lina (sec): post-incident action items (short): ["create RBAC least-privilege task","add KMS usage alerting","add auto-rotation playbook with safety checks","customer key rotation template","run vuln triage on onboarding token mint flow"]. I'll own RBAC task.
